Convention: a ring is commutative with $1$; an $R$-algebra is associative, unital and central over $R$.

Let $R$ be a ring. Let $(B, \text{d})$ be a differential graded $R$-algebra.
There exists a quasi-isomorphism $(A, \text{d}) \to (B, \text{d})$ of
differential graded $R$-algebras with the following properties
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A$ is K-flat as a complex of $R$-modules,
\item $A$ is a free graded $R$-algebra.
\end{enumerate}

reason: Constructs a free graded tensor dg algebra on cocycles surjecting onto H*(B), then iteratively adjoins free generators with prescribed boundaries to kill the cohomological kernel. The directed union remains graded-free and K-flat, and every kernel class dies at the next stage, giving a quasi-isomorphism.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Convention: a ring is commutative with $1$; an $R$-algebra is associative, unital and central over $R$.

Let $R$ be a ring. Let $(A, \text{d})$, $(B, \text{d})$, and
$(C, \text{d})$ be differential graded $R$-algebras. Assume
$A \otimes_R C$ represents $A \otimes^\mathbf{L}_R C$ in $D(R)$.
Let $N$ be a differential graded $(A, B)$-bimodule.
Let $N'$ be a differential graded $(B, C)$-bimodule.
Then the composition
$$
\xymatrix{
D(A, \text{d}) \ar[rr]^{- \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} N} & &
D(B, \text{d}) \ar[rr]^{- \otimes_B^\mathbf{L} N'} & &
D(C, \text{d})
}
$$
is isomorphic to $- \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} N''$ for some differential graded
$(A, C)$-bimodule $N''$.
hypotheses:
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $(A, \text{d})$, $(B, \text{d})$, and
$(C, \text{d})$ be differential graded $R$-algebras. Assume
$A \otimes_R C$ represents $A \otimes^\mathbf{L}_R C$ in $D(R)$.
Let $N$ be a differential graded $(A, B)$-bimodule.
Let $N'$ be a differential graded $(B, C)$-bimodule.
conclusions:
the composition
$$
\xymatrix{
D(A, \text{d}) \ar[rr]^{- \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} N} & &
D(B, \text{d}) \ar[rr]^{- \otimes_B^\mathbf{L} N'} & &
D(C, \text{d})
}
$$
is isomorphic to $- \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} N''$ for some differential graded
$(A, C)$-bimodule $N''$.

reason: The proof reduces via a K-flat resolution B'→B and then tries to show the derived/plain comparison for A⊗_R B⊗_R C. However at line 7043 it defines P=L⊗_R B, while line 7053 rewrites P⊗_B(B⊗_R C) as P⊗_R B⊗_R C instead of L⊗_R B⊗_R C; line 7061 similarly uses P⊗_R C where the hypothesis concerns L⊗_R C. These symbol substitutions leave the decisive quasi-isomorphism implication unclear without source correction.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $(A, \text{d})$ be a differential graded algebra with
$H^i(A)$ countable for each $i$. Let $M$ be an object of $D(A, \text{d})$.
Then the following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $M = \text{hocolim} E_n$ with $E_n$ compact in $D(A, \text{d})$, and
\item $H^i(M)$ is countable for each $i$.
\end{enumerate}
hypotheses:
Let $(A, \text{d})$ be a differential graded algebra with
$H^i(A)$ countable for each $i$. Let $M$ be an object of $D(A, \text{d})$.

reason: For compact-cell homotopy colimits, countability follows from finite-cell cohomology and sequential colimits. Conversely, constructs a countable quasi-isomorphic dg subalgebra A' and a countable property-(P) resolution of M, then expresses that resolution as an increasing union of finite dg subcell modules. Each finite subcell is compact and their homotopy colimit recovers M.
